name: DUSRSECJ.jcl
description:
This JCL job (DUSRSECJ) initializes the User Security (USRSEC) VSAM file for the CardDemo application by creating and loading user credentials for both administrative and regular users. It first creates a flat sequential file with 10 predefined user records (5 administrators and 5 regular users), then rebuilds the VSAM KSDS cluster, and finally loads all user records into it.Key Functionalities:
Deletes any pre-existing temporary sequential file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS) to ensure a clean start before processing.
Creates a new sequential flat file containing exactly 10 user records: 5 administrator accounts (ADMIN001–ADMIN005) and 5 regular user accounts (USER0001–USER0005), each with first name, last name, and password, stored as fixed-length 80-byte records.
Deletes the existing VSAM KSDS cluster (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS) and redefines it with an 8-byte key starting at position 0, fixed 80-byte record size, indexed organization, and allocated space of 45 primary and 15 secondary tracks.
Loads all 10 user security records from the sequential flat file into the newly created VSAM KSDS cluster, establishing the initial user security reference data for the CardDemo application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security staging file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS) may or may not exist in the system from a prior execution of the initialization job
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The pre-deletion cleanup step is triggered at the start of the User Security database initialization job
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Security staging file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS) must be deleted if it exists — whether the cleanup step completes successfully or encounters an error — ensuring no residual or stale user security data remains before the new file is created; if the file does not exist, the step must complete successfully without raising an error, allowing the job to continue normally

rules.Rule_Name: PREDEL - IEFBR14 - Pre-Initialization Cleanup of User Security Staging File
rules.Rule_Description: Before creating a fresh User Security staging file, any previously existing version of the file must be unconditionally removed to ensure the initialization process always starts from a clean state. This applies whether the job is being run for the first time or is being re-executed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user security record is being created for the CardDemo User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record is written to the User Security flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record must be exactly 80 characters long, structured as: User ID occupying characters 1–8, First Name occupying characters 9–28 (space-padded to 20 characters), Last Name occupying characters 29–48 (space-padded to 20 characters), Password occupying characters 49–57 (9 characters), and remaining characters 58–80 filled with spaces

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Define User Security Record Structure
rules.Rule_Description: Each user security record stored in the User Security file must follow a fixed 80-character layout with defined fields for User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user account is designated as an Administrator in the CardDemo system
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Administrator's User ID is assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID must be exactly 8 characters long, beginning with the prefix 'ADMIN' followed by a 3-digit zero-padded sequence number (e.g., ADMIN001, ADMIN002, ADMIN003, ADMIN004, ADMIN005)

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Define Administrator User Account Identity
rules.Rule_Description: Administrator user accounts in the CardDemo system are identified by a specific User ID format that combines a role prefix and a 3-digit sequence number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user account is designated as a Regular User in the CardDemo system
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Regular User's User ID is assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID must be exactly 8 characters long, beginning with the prefix 'USER' followed by a 4-digit zero-padded sequence number (e.g., USER0001, USER0002, USER0003, USER0004, USER0005)

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Define Regular User Account Identity
rules.Rule_Description: Regular user accounts in the CardDemo system are identified by a specific User ID format that combines a role prefix and a 4-digit sequence number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user account has a User ID beginning with the prefix 'ADMIN' (i.e., the account is an Administrator)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The password is assigned to the Administrator account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The password must be 'PASSWORDA' — the suffix 'A' designates the Administrator role

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Assign Administrator Password Convention
rules.Rule_Description: Administrator accounts must be assigned a password that follows the Administrator password convention, distinguishing them from Regular User passwords.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user account has a User ID beginning with the prefix 'USER' (i.e., the account is a Regular User)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The password is assigned to the Regular User account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The password must be 'PASSWORDU' — the suffix 'U' designates the Regular User role

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Assign Regular User Password Convention
rules.Rule_Description: Regular user accounts must be assigned a password that follows the Regular User password convention, distinguishing them from Administrator passwords.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security system is being initialized for the first time or reset
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security file is created
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Exactly 5 Administrator accounts must be created with the following identities: (1) ADMIN001 — MARGARET GOLD, (2) ADMIN002 — RUSSELL RUSSELL, (3) ADMIN003 — RAYMOND WHITMORE, (4) ADMIN004 — EMMANUEL CASGRAIN, (5) ADMIN005 — GRANVILLE LACHAPELLE; all with password PASSWORDA

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Seed Initial Administrator Accounts
rules.Rule_Description: The CardDemo User Security system must be initialized with exactly 5 predefined Administrator accounts with their full names.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security system is being initialized for the first time or reset
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security file is created
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Exactly 5 Regular User accounts must be created with the following identities: (1) USER0001 — LAWRENCE THOMAS, (2) USER0002 — AJITH KUMAR, (3) USER0003 — LAURITZ ALME, (4) USER0004 — AVERARDO MAZZI, (5) USER0005 — LEE TING; all with password PASSWORDU

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Seed Initial Regular User Accounts
rules.Rule_Description: The CardDemo User Security system must be initialized with exactly 5 predefined Regular User accounts with their full names.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The 10 predefined user security records (5 Administrators and 5 Regular Users) are ready to be written to the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS) is created
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 records must be copied to the output file exactly as-is with no transformation applied; the output file must be a new file registered in the system catalog upon successful completion, and if the file creation fails, no partial file must be retained

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Create User Security Flat File Without Transformation
rules.Rule_Description: User security records must be written to the User Security flat file exactly as defined, with no modification, filtering, or reformatting applied during the file creation process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security database initialization process has been triggered for the CardDemo application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the DELETE command targeting the User Security database named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The existing User Security database — including all stored user records, the data component (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS.DAT), and the index component (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS.IDX) — is completely removed from the system, ensuring no residual user data carries over into the new database

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - Existing User Security Database Removal
rules.Rule_Description: Before creating a fresh User Security database, any previously existing version must be completely removed, including all stored user records, the data store, and the index.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE command for the User Security database has been executed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security database did not exist prior to the deletion attempt — meaning this is either a first-time setup or the database was already removed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error raised by the failed deletion is suppressed by resetting the condition code to zero (SET MAXCC = 0), and the process continues forward to database creation without failure — the absence of a prior database is treated as a valid and acceptable state

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - First-Time Initialization Error Suppression
rules.Rule_Description: When the User Security database does not yet exist (e.g., first-time environment setup), the deletion attempt would normally raise an error and halt processing. This rule ensures the initialization continues gracefully in that scenario.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security VSAM database is being created via the DEFINE CLUSTER command
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key structure is defined using KEYS(8,0)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first 8 characters of every user record — representing the User ID (e.g., ADMIN001, USER0001) — are designated as the unique lookup key starting at position 1 of the record; no two users may share the same User ID, and the CardDemo application can retrieve any user record directly and instantly using their User ID

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - User ID as Unique Database Lookup Key
rules.Rule_Description: The User Security database must be structured so that every user record is uniquely identified and retrievable by their User ID, which occupies the first 8 characters of each record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security VSAM database is being created via the DEFINE CLUSTER command
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record size is defined using RECORDSIZE(80,80) — setting both the minimum and maximum record length to 80 characters
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Every user security record stored in the database must be exactly 80 characters in length; records shorter or longer than 80 characters are not permitted, enforcing a uniform fixed-length structure for all user accounts including User ID, First Name, Last Name, Password, and padding

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - Fixed 80-Character User Record Size Enforcement
rules.Rule_Description: Every user security record stored in the database must conform to a strict fixed-length structure of exactly 80 characters to ensure consistent data layout across all user accounts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security VSAM database is being created via the DEFINE CLUSTER command
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The REUSE attribute is applied during database creation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database is configured to allow its contents to be completely replaced and reloaded in future initialization runs without needing to redefine the database structure — enabling the initialization job to be safely re-executed multiple times to refresh user security data

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - User Security Database Reusability for Repeated Initialization
rules.Rule_Description: The User Security database must be designed to support repeated initialization runs — allowing the database to be fully reloaded with fresh user data in future executions without requiring structural redefinition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security VSAM database is being created via the DEFINE CLUSTER command
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The free space parameters are applied using FREESPACE(10,15)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database reserves 10% free space within each individual data block and 15% free space within each larger storage area; this reserved capacity allows new user records to be added to the database in the future without disrupting the existing data layout or requiring a full database rebuild

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - Free Space Reservation for Future User Additions
rules.Rule_Description: The User Security database must reserve internal free space at the time of creation to accommodate future user record insertions without requiring database reorganization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security VSAM database is being created via the DEFINE CLUSTER command
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The INDEXED organization is specified and separate component names are assigned — DATA component named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS.DAT and INDEX component named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS.IDX
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The database maintains user records in User ID sequence within the data store (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS.DAT) and maintains a separate index structure (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS.IDX) that maps each User ID to its corresponding record location — enabling the CardDemo application to retrieve any user's security record directly and efficiently using their User ID without scanning all records

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - Indexed User Security Database Structure with Separate Data and Index Components
rules.Rule_Description: The User Security database must be organized as an indexed structure with physically separate data and index components, enabling the CardDemo application to perform fast, direct user lookups by User ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security sequential flat file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.PS) exists and contains all 10 predefined user records (5 Administrators and 5 Regular Users), AND the User Security VSAM database (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.KSDS) has been defined and is empty and ready to receive records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The bulk load process is triggered to transfer all records from the User Security flat file into the User Security VSAM database, reading every record sequentially from the flat file and inserting each one into the indexed database using the User ID (first 8 characters of each record) as the unique lookup key, with no filtering, transformation, or conditional selection applied — every record is loaded exactly as stored
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 user security records are successfully inserted into the User Security VSAM database indexed by User ID, making all Administrator accounts (ADMIN001–ADMIN005) and all Regular User accounts (USER0001–USER0005) fully accessible for authentication and role-based access control within the CardDemo application; the database is now the active, searchable source of user security information

rules.Rule_Name: STEP03 - IDCAMS - Bulk Load of User Security Records into User Security Database
rules.Rule_Description: All predefined user security records stored in the User Security sequential flat file are loaded in full into the User Security VSAM database, making every user account available for authentication and access control within the CardDemo application.
